title: A Sigil for the Garden
premise: Lena Villalobos, a mercenary of the silent god Veyra, discovers the old gods' return is no miracle: the usurper Malachar has caged them beneath Thornfell and is harvesting their voices to fuel his armies. Among the stolen souls sold to his subterranean court is Ilsa, Lena's sister, whose memory was traded away years ago in a bargain Lena made to survive. Guided by a smuggler's map written in sigils only the faithful can read, Lena descends through the mountain's smuggler roads with a defrocked priest and a turncoat courtier. In the climax she shatters the god-cage, learning that Veyra's silence was a sacrifice made to hide her — for Lena herself carries the final sigil that can free or enslave all the old gods. Choosing truth over loyalty, Lena releases the gods at the cost of her own memories of Ilsa, and the freed deities break Malachar's armies as the free cities rise.
about_author: Zephyrine Thornbury is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons leading treks through mountain passes before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy rooted in the geography of borders, smuggling routes, and the small bargains people make to cross them.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: POV Lena. On a rain-slicked contract job in the foothills, Lena prays to Veyra out of habit and hears nothing — again. When her employer's caravan is ambushed by soldiers bearing a new sigil, she realizes the old roads are changing hands. Emotional beat: weary resignation hardening into unease.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Lena. A dying smuggler presses a sigil-marked map into Lena's hands, whispering that the gods are 'singing under the stone.' Soldiers burn the waystation behind her. Emotional beat: grief and the first pull of destiny she wants to refuse.

chapters.title: What the Free Cities Remember
chapters.summary: POV Lena. In the city of Corvale, temples are reopening overnight; crowds weep at answered prayers. Lena's mercenary company debates which side to sell to. Her captain orders her to deliver the map to Malachar's agents. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against instinct.

chapters.title: The Defrocked Priest
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Anselm, a priest cast out for claiming the gods were prisoners rather than departed, recognizes the sigil map and begs Lena to take him east. She refuses; he follows anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual stubbornness.

chapters.title: A Bargain Already Paid
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Flashback woven into present: ten years ago Lena sold her sister Ilsa's soul to a broker beneath the mountain to buy her own freedom from a death-debt. Now she learns where souls go when they're sold. Emotional beat: buried guilt surfacing like a wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Courtier Sera Vane, fleeing Malachar's court with proof of the god-cage, intercepts Lena on the Salt Road. She offers passage through the mountain's inner ways in exchange for protection. Emotional beat: wary negotiation between two women who trust nothing.

chapters.title: Roads That Move
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The three travel the shifting smuggler roads, guided by sigils that glow brighter as they near Thornfell. Anselm teaches Lena the old prayers; one of them makes the mountain answer. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Malachar's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Sera. At a border fort, Sera reveals Malachar speaks with the borrowed voice of a dead god, and his armies cannot be broken while he wears it. Lena realizes the usurper knows about the map — and about her. Emotional beat: the hunt becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Company Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena's former captain catches up with a kill order. Lena refuses to hand over the map and fights her way out, wounding a friend. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing a path — loneliness as payment.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Sheltering in a shrine cave, Anselm confesses he once served the broker who bought Ilsa's soul, and that he has been searching for her ever since. Lena's fury nearly ends the journey. Emotional beat: rage giving way, barely, to shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the Falls
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The sigil map leads them to a hidden gate behind a frozen waterfall, sealed with Veyra's mark — the first time her silent god has left any sign in a decade. Emotional beat: hope arriving so suddenly it feels like vertigo.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: POV Sera. The three enter the mountain's interior: a vast inverted court lit by captive godlight, where sold souls serve as currency and ornament. Sera navigates its etiquette while Lena sees what a soul looks like after it's spent. Emotional beat: horror wearing beautiful clothes.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Lena. To find Ilsa, Lena must trade a memory of equal weight. She offers her memory of her mother's face; the broker accepts but warns the ledger balances both ways. Emotional beat: sacrifice as transaction, love measured in loss.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena finds Ilsa serving in the court's galleries — alive, hollow-eyed, remembering nothing of her. Ilsa mistakes her for a stranger and asks her name twice. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharper than any blade.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Malachar summons them, courteous and terrible, offering Lena command of his armies if she surrenders the map. He reveals the cage's true function: the gods sing the world's boundaries into being, and he means to rewrite them. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as ambition.

chapters.title: What Veyra Hid
chapters.summary: POV Lena. In the cage's depths, Lena finds Veyra diminished but conscious — and learns the truth: Veyra went silent to hide the final sigil inside Lena herself, placed there at her birth. The gods' freedom lives or dies in her blood. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade in a single breath.

chapters.title: The Choice of Loyalties
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Malachar's forces close in; Sera is captured covering their retreat. Anselm urges Lena to flee with Ilsa and let the world fend for itself. Lena must weigh her sister against every stranger the rewritten world would unmake. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: Breaking the Cage
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena sings the final sigil aloud, shattering the god-cage as Malachar's armies storm the court. Freed gods pour their voices back into the world; the mountain itself convulses. Emotional beat: catharsis through ruin.

chapters.title: The Price of the Song
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The released gods demand balance: the sigil's power must be paid from its bearer. Lena surrenders her memories of Ilsa — every one — to complete the breaking. Ilsa, restored, watches her sister forget her. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Armies Unmade
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Above ground, the god-voiced armies fall silent mid-march as Malachar loses his stolen voice; the free cities' militias, led by Lena's old company turned coat, rout them. Sera frees herself in the chaos. Emotional beat: triumph earned secondhand, witnessed from the field.

chapters.title: Two Strangers on a Road
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena wakes in Corvale with gaps in her past and a sister she doesn't recognize insisting on walking beside her anyway. Ilsa begins telling her their childhood, story by story, as an offering. Emotional beat: quiet, stubborn hope.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Garden
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Months later, Lena plants a garden above the sealed mountain gate, marking it with Veyra's sigil — now a blessing rather than a burden. The gods answer prayers gently now, and hers most softly of all. Emotional beat: peace as a choice renewed daily.
